symptom: An IF/ELSE as the last statement of a loop or while body got an ExclusiveMerge with no outgoing flow: both branches end the iteration, so it joined nothing. Studio Pro authors delete it by hand (the reporter's hand-polished flow had 2 merges, mxcli's rebuild of the same MDL 4), and since describe printed the same MDL with and without it, every re-exec drew it again.
cause: addIfStatement decided needMerge from returns alone; the loop-body loops in addLoopStatement/addWhileStatement never told a statement it was last, so nothing knew the IF's continuation was the end of the iteration
file: mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_control.go (atBodyTail, addIfStatement tailWithoutMerge, both loop-body loops), cmd_microflows_builder.go (flowBuilder.atBodyTail), cmd_microflows_show_helpers.go (emitMergeAnnotation)
insight: The claim the fix rests on — Mendix accepts two dead-end branches at a loop tail — was run, not assumed: PedApp 11.13 with the shape built gives the identical mx check error set to the pristine copy, and Studio Pro 11.15's ped_check_errors reports none. Keep the merge when either branch is empty (a split needs a flow per case: CE0079), when a branch ends in a continuing custom error handler, and when @merge is written; pass the tail on to the last statement of each branch so a nested IF/ELSE at the tail loses its merge too. The read side is the trap: a stored tail merge (an earlier mxcli's) sits at the OLD derived position, so the canonical describe treated its @merge as derivable and dropped it, and the rebuild then removed the node — emitMergeAnnotation now always states @merge for a split merge with no way out. assertDescriptionRebuildsGraph compares graphs modulo merges and cannot see any of this; count merges.
